en.content:
The Tai Po Wang Fuk Court fire has become more than a tragedy of loss—it is now a test of Hong Kong’s public administration, particularly how the city listens, responds, and translates grief into lasting safeguards. Survivors’ repeated petitions to senior officials within a week signal both urgency and frustration: while the immediate rescue and investigation matter, families are asking for something equally concrete—whether the government can rebuild on site and do so transparently, with clear timelines and meaningful participation from those most affected.

Yet petitions should not be allowed to drift into spectacle. As Beijing has cautioned against “politicising” the disaster to “stir up chaos,” the most constructive path is to treat every claim and every evidence strand as part of a rigorous, apolitical review—covering building safety, emergency response, and relief support. Hong Kong’s governance strength lies in turning inquiry findings into engineering decisions and policy refinements, rather than allowing competing narratives to overshadow the shared goal of preventing recurrence.

What matters most now is whether public processes are designed for accountability and speed. The emergence of multiple public-hearing accounts—including survivors describing final calls with loved ones—underscores the human stakes behind administrative failures and communication breakdowns. Government bodies should therefore prioritise: timely disclosure of investigation conclusions; a clear plan for redevelopment arrangements; assistance that is accessible and not overly bureaucratic; and verifiable safety standards for both the construction phase and future residents.

Finally, Hong Kong should learn from this tragedy in a way that improves daily life, not only immediate outcomes. A redevelopment promise must be paired with stronger building governance, better emergency readiness, and sustained welfare support until families can restart their lives with confidence. If the authorities respond with practical measures that respect victims’ dignity and restore public trust, the city can honour the victims not through argument, but through results.
en.topic_title: Tai Po fire survivors petition top Hong Kong officials twice in week for on-site redevelopment

zh.content:
大埔王福法院火災倖存者一再向本港最高層施壓，並要求「原址重建」，其實講的不單是屋苑安排，而係一個社會對公義、對生命尊嚴、同對災後處理程序嘅最低期望。當災後重建被拖慢，受影響家庭就會被迫長時間活喺不確定之中：身心創傷未復，生活重建亦無依歸。倖存者兩次即日常般嘅請願行動，反映出佢哋對制度溝通、資訊透明度、同決策方向感到不夠有保障——呢種失望唔應該只用一句「會跟進」去消化。

同時，原址重建背後亦係城市規劃同社會連結嘅問題：唔少居民喺呢度生活多年，社區網絡、日常交通節奏、甚至對環境熟悉度，都係重建成敗嘅關鍵。若以「撤離、另覓地、重來」作為預設方案，固然有可能涉及土地、建築流程同安全評估，但當相關資訊未能及時、清晰、具體咁交代，居民就會自然認為政府程序優先，家庭權益次之。對於當事人而言，最重要嘅唔係爭口舌，而係能否盡快得到可落地嘅承諾：時間表、安置方案、賠償與支援機制，以及為何唔選擇原址重建之間嘅理據。

不過，任何一個災後決策，都必須建立喺可驗證嘅安全標準同獨立調查結果之上。倖存者要求原址重建，亦唔等於忽視風險；反而合理做法係：公開重建可行性評估、展示工程設計如何回應火災致因與逃生要求、同時確保過渡安置唔再被動挨批評。政府同相關部門應該同時做到兩件事：一方面尊重居民訴求，給予清楚方案與時間表；另一方面亦要確保監管與執行能夠經得起追問，唔好令「救火式」處理變成「長尾式」折磨。

最後，當火災成為政治動員或情緒爭拗嘅題材，社會其實只會更難聚焦真正嘅核心——即係死傷者應得嘅交代、倖存者應得嘅支援、同城市安全應有嘅改造。可以理解內地及本港各方對維穩與秩序嘅關注，但亦應明白：倖存者追求原址重建，本質係對生活與尊嚴嘅合理要求，而非「製造混亂」。若當局願意用更透明、更具體、更可量度嘅方式回應，將能把公眾訴求由情緒拉回制度解決，亦令每一個家庭相信——災難之後，社會唔會只顧「過咗就算」，而係會真正「改善到位」。

en.topic_title: Tai Po fire survivors petition top Hong Kong officials twice in week for on-site redevelopment
en.topic_summary:
A group of survivors of the deadly Wang Fuk Court fire have petitioned Hong Kong’s top officials twice in a week, urging the government to rebuild the fire-ravaged residential estate on site and to respect their private property rights.



According to copies of the petitions received by HKFP on Thursday, the petitioners sent the letters to a group of top officials on Wednesday this week and last week, asking them to reconsider the in-situ redevelopment of Wang Fuk Court.



Wang Fuk Court
